headline: The same testosterone dose
body: Depending on how much you give and how old you are.
punch: Which means two people on identical protocols get different hormones.

headline: Testosterone
body: Part becomes estradiol through aromatase. Part becomes DHT through 5-alpha-reductase. What remains stays testosterone.

headline: Researchers measured
body: In men, directly measuring how testosterone dose and patient age affect the proportion converted to estradiol versus DHT.

headline: Dose changes
body: The conversion fractions are not fixed. Raising the dose does not scale all three hormones by the same multiplier.
punch: Double the dose is not double everything.

headline: And age changes it
body: Patient age independently affects the conversion pattern — so the same milligram amount produces a different hormonal profile at different ages.

headline: Why this matters here
body: Estradiol is the dominant driver of growth plate closure. Anything raising the aromatised fraction is spending skeletal maturation, whatever the intention was.
punch: The conversion fraction is the part that closes plates.

headline: Which makes
body: A protocol described as producing one hormonal state produces a different one at another dose or another age — and the difference lands exactly on the closure mechanism.
punch: The number transfers. The outcome doesn't.

headline: The useful takeaway
body: When you see any androgen protocol, the question isn't the milligrams. It's what fraction becomes estradiol in that person — and that isn't on the label.
punch: Ask what it becomes, not what it is.
